stimuli.title: Meridian: the Ridgeline acquisition
stimuli.text: Two years after the ATM breach, Meridian Financial is buying Ridgeline Savings, a 40-branch thrift with its own core banking platform and a customer analytics contract with a processor in Bangalore. The deal signs in six weeks. Ridgeline has never had a CISO, and its board minutes record one penetration test, in 2021. Meridian's board has told the CISO that security must not delay the closing. The examiner will review the combined entity nine months after close. Ridgeline's analytics contract renews automatically thirty days after any change of control.

profile.organization: Meridian Financial Services · acquiring Ridgeline Savings, 40 branches
profile.regime: GLBA · state breach notification · examination nine months after close
profile.environment: Two core banking platforms · Ridgeline analytics processor in Bangalore
profile.state: Six weeks to signing, no security due diligence performed

stimuli.title: Meridian: the document set
stimuli.text: Meridian's new CISO inherits a document set that grew by accident. There is a thirty-page information security policy last approved in 2019, four standards that contradict it on password length, a wiki of procedures written by whoever last did the task, and a recommended practices page nobody can say is binding. The board approved the policy; nobody can say who approved the standards. Meanwhile two branch regions are merging and 300 staff are changing roles, and the awareness programme still teaches a threat catalogue written before the bank used any cloud service at all.

profile.regime: GLBA · PCI DSS · state banking examination
profile.environment: Policy approved 2019 · four conflicting standards · procedures on a wiki
profile.state: 300 staff changing roles during a branch-region merger

stimuli.title: Nexus: the platform split
stimuli.text: Nexus Bank is replacing the fleet-management platform that administers its SlimLine terminals. Today it is one Windows server in the bank's own data center. The target design splits it four ways: a browser console for branch staff, an application tier of Linux containers on a shared cluster, event-driven functions at a cloud provider that reconcile cash balances overnight, and the legacy dispenser-control service, which nobody will rewrite and which will run as a guest on the bank's hypervisor. The migration board has ten weeks and no budget for a second cluster. Security must sign off on each tier separately, and the board meets once a month.

profile.organization: Nexus Bank · SlimLine subway ATM fleet
profile.environment: Browser console · shared container cluster · cloud functions · one hypervisor
profile.state: Ten weeks to migrate, four tiers to sign off separately

stimuli.title: Nexus: the SlimLine II programme
stimuli.text: Two years after the shim attack, Nexus Bank has funded a replacement terminal, the SlimLine II. The programme board meets monthly and has just approved the architecture. Three decisions are still open: how the security requirements become a concrete control set, how the new dispenser interface will be joined to the existing transaction switch, and how 900 SlimLine units leave service. The bank's examiner has asked for evidence at each gate. Finance wants the retired units sold to a secondary-market refurbisher, which pays considerably more than a recycler does and collects from the branch loading dock.

profile.organization: Nexus Bank · SlimLine II replacement programme
profile.environment: 900 SlimLine units in service · new dispenser interface · existing transaction switch
profile.state: Architecture approved, control set not yet chosen

stimuli.title: QuickCash: after SuperAdmin
stimuli.text: Six months after the SuperAdmin theft, QuickCash has replaced the shared account with named identities and is rebuilding everything around it. Its directory runs on two domain controllers in the regional office, and the ATM management console authenticates against them. The board has bought a cloud service desk and a cloud expense tool, and both want their own logins. The five field technicians need administrative rights on the console, but only while a work order is open. The regional manager who created SuperAdmin still signs off every access request. The next audit closes in eight weeks.

profile.organization: QuickCash Inc · 300 ATMs, five field technicians
profile.environment: Two on-premises domain controllers · ATM management console · two new cloud applications
profile.state: Eight weeks to audit, access model half rebuilt

stimuli.title: FinCorp: the second report
stimuli.text: Nine days after the negative-deposit story broke, FinCorp's security mailbox receives a second report. An independent researcher writes that the same mobile deposit endpoint accepts an amount carrying sixteen decimal places, and that the balance service rounds it in the customer's favour. She has not published, gives a ninety-day deadline, and asks for a named contact. FinCorp has no vulnerability disclosure policy, no bug bounty, and no stated position on researchers who test its live application. The VP of Engineering who waived the gate review still owns the release schedule. Legal's first draft reply threatens action under the terms of service.

profile.organization: FinCorp · mobile check deposit for ATM customers
profile.regime: State banking examination · card brand rules
profile.environment: Mobile deposit endpoint · balance service · no disclosure policy
profile.state: Day nine after a related flaw went public, second report in hand

stimuli.title: Global Bank: the pipeline rebuild
stimuli.text: Global Bank is rebuilding the Cardless Cash pipeline it had when a master key reached a public repository. The new design keeps the same three teams and the same weekly release. Secrets move to a managed vault. Builds run on shared runners any team can queue work on, and the repository is private, but every developer can push to the main branch. Nobody can currently say which build produced the artefact running in production. The bank's examiner has asked for evidence that the pipeline enforces the bank's own rules, not merely that the rules exist somewhere.

profile.organization: Global Bank · Cardless Cash mobile app and API
profile.environment: Private repository · shared build runners · weekly release · managed secret vault
profile.state: Pipeline rebuild after a hardcoded key reached a public repository

stimuli.title: Global ATM: the Toledo prompt
stimuli.text: Eight months after the patch outage, Global ATM Corp's service desk logs a report from a branch: an ATM in Toledo displayed a command prompt for a few seconds during a maintenance visit. The fleet runs a standard Windows build with anti-malware and a monthly patch cycle. Each machine writes its own event log locally and keeps thirty days of it. There is no rule about which programs may run. The maintenance vendor's technician says he ran a diagnostic tool he downloaded that morning. By the time an analyst calls back, the machine has been rebooted twice.

profile.environment: Standard Windows build · local event logs, 30 days · outsourced maintenance
profile.state: One reported command prompt, machine already rebooted twice

stimuli.title: Global ATM: two exercises
stimuli.text: A year after the outage, Global ATM Corp has a written disaster recovery plan for the transaction switch and has run one tabletop against it. The plan names a recovery team of eleven people across three time zones, lists a call tree, and assumes the switch can be brought up at the Columbus site within four hours. Nobody has yet performed any of the steps. The board has approved two exercises this year and will not accept an outage of production. The operations director has asked what the two exercises should be and what evidence each will produce.

profile.regime: State banking examination · card brand availability requirements
profile.environment: Transaction switch · alternate site at Columbus · eleven-person recovery team, three time zones
profile.state: Plan written, one tabletop run, no procedure yet performed

questionsV2.question: The board has said security must not delay the closing. Which contribution to the acquisition process is the BEST use of the CISO's remaining six weeks?

options.A: Withhold approval of the transaction until Ridgeline's controls match Meridian's.
options.B: Defer the security review until after close, when Meridian controls the systems.
options.C: Complete a full control assessment of Ridgeline before the six weeks expire.
options.D: Quantify Ridgeline's security risk so the board can price it into the deal.

questionsV2.explanation: An acquisition is a risk transfer with a price attached, and the only lever available before signing is the price. A number the board can put next to the purchase price is worth more than an objection it will overrule. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SA-4 Acquisition Process requires security and privacy requirements to be included in the contract for the thing being acquired, and PM-30 Supply Chain Risk Management Strategy sets the organization-wide approach behind it. NIST SP 800-161 Rev 1 (upd 1) Section 3.1 treats acquisition as the moment when a supplier's posture becomes the acquirer's exposure. A is not the decision-maker's, because the board owns the transaction and the CISO informs it. B is wrong phase: after close the risk is owned, the price is fixed and the leverage is gone. C is wrong scope, since six weeks buys material findings rather than a complete assessment, and demanding the impossible is how security gets left out of the next deal. Price the risk instead of blocking the deal.
questionsV2.recallLine: The board will not let security delay a closing. What is the best use of six weeks?

optionsShort.C: Full control assessment in six weeks

A.label: not the decision-maker's
A.wouldAnswer: Who decides whether a transaction proceeds when the risk is judged unacceptable?

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: What work genuinely does belong to the integration period rather than to due diligence?

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: What would the CISO scope if the deal timetable were nine months instead of six weeks?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SA-4 Acquisition Process; PM-30 Supply Chain Risk Management Strategy
NIST SP 800-161 Rev 1 (upd 1) | Section 3.1 C-SCRM in Acquisition

questionsV2.question: Ridgeline's analytics contract renews automatically thirty days after any change of control. Which action MOST reduces the risk Meridian inherits with it?

options.A: Add the processor to Meridian's vendor register with an annual review.
options.B: Use the change-of-control window to renegotiate security terms before renewal.
options.C: Require the processor to complete Meridian's standard security questionnaire.
options.D: Obtain the processor's most recent third-party audit report from Ridgeline.

questionsV2.explanation: A supplier contract is easiest to change at the one moment it is open, and this one is open for thirty days and then shut for a term nobody at Meridian negotiated. Everything else on the list can be done in month four; only B expires. NIST SP 800-161 Rev 1 (upd 1) Section 3.1 places supply-chain requirements in the acquisition and contracting activity for exactly this reason, and NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SR-3 Supply Chain Controls and Processes, SR-5 Acquisition Strategies, Tools, and Methods and SA-9 External System Services are where the requirements land. Note that the copy of SP 800-161 Rev 1 in circulation carries a NIST notice superseding it with the Rev 1 errata update, which renumbers nothing. A is wrong phase, a steady-state process applied to a moment that closes. C is correct but not first, evidence gathering while the leverage expires. D is the right control for a different problem, describing the processor's controls without changing Meridian's position. Move while the door is open.
questionsV2.recallLine: An inherited vendor contract auto-renews in thirty days. What most reduces the inherited risk?

optionsShort.A: Add to vendor register, annual review
optionsShort.B: Renegotiate terms in the open window

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: How should this processor be governed once its contract terms are settled?

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: How does Meridian assess a supplier whose contract is not about to renew?

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: What evidence should Meridian collect to judge whether the processor's controls are adequate?

sources: NIST SP 800-161 Rev 1 (upd 1) | Section 3.1 C-SCRM in Acquisition
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SR-3 Supply Chain Controls and Processes; SR-5 Acquisition Strategies, Tools, and Methods; SA-9 External System Services

questionsV2.question: The analytics dataset includes EU residents who bank at two Ridgeline branches, and the processor is in Bangalore. Which requirement applies MOST directly to that flow?

options.A: The data must be encrypted in transit and at rest throughout the processing chain.
options.B: The processor must be named in Meridian's incident response plan as a notification party.
options.C: The transfer needs an adequacy decision, appropriate safeguards, or a stated derogation.
options.D: The dataset must be reduced to the minimum fields the analytics contract requires.

questionsV2.explanation: Personal data leaving the European Economic Area needs a lawful basis for the transfer itself, separate from any basis for processing it. Chapter V of the General Data Protection Regulation, Regulation (EU) 2016/679, states the general principle at Article 44, adequacy decisions for a destination country at Article 45, appropriate safeguards including standard contractual clauses and binding corporate rules at Article 46, and the narrow derogations at Article 49. Onward transfers must not undermine the protection. On the control side, NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CM-12 Information Location and SA-9(5) External System Services | Processing, Storage, and Service Location are how an organization knows and restricts where its data physically sits. A is the right control for a different problem: encryption protects the data and does not make the transfer lawful. B is wrong scope, an incident-handling arrangement rather than a transfer basis. D is correct but not first, since minimisation is a genuine obligation that reduces exposure without supplying a basis. Lawfulness first, then protection.
questionsV2.recallLine: An offshore processor handles EU residents' data. Which requirement applies most directly to the transfer?

optionsShort.A: Encrypt in transit and at rest
optionsShort.B: Name the processor in the IR plan

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: What protects the dataset against interception or theft along the processing chain?

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: What must be arranged so a processor's breach reaches Meridian's responders quickly?

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: What principle limits how much personal data a processor should receive at all?

sources: EU GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) | Chapter V, Articles 44, 45, 46 and 49
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-12 Information Location; SA-9(5) Processing, Storage, and Service Location

questionsV2.question: At the examination nine months after close, the examiner asks how Meridian satisfied itself about Ridgeline. Which pair of facts BEST evidences due diligence and due care?

options.A: The pre-close risk assessment, and the assessments run on Ridgeline's systems since close.
options.B: The signed purchase agreement, and the security clauses Meridian wrote into it.
options.C: Ridgeline's 2021 penetration test, and Meridian's remediation plan for its findings.
options.D: Meridian's own examination record, and the policy set now applied to both entities.

questionsV2.explanation: The pair is a sequence, not a synonym. Due diligence is the investigation made before a commitment; due care is the continuing exercise of oversight after it, and an examiner asking about both wants evidence from each side of the closing date. Only A supplies both. NIST SP 800-161 Rev 1 (upd 1) Section 3.1 describes the pre-contract investigation, and NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SR-6 Supplier Assessments and Reviews carries the ongoing half. Worth saying plainly: no NIST document defines the due care and due diligence pair, which is a legal liability concept rather than a controls concept, so an answer that leans on a control number alone has missed the question. B is wrong scope, evidencing what was agreed rather than what was investigated or overseen. C is wrong phase, a four-year-old test that predates the transaction and records Ridgeline's activity, not Meridian's. D is the right control for a different problem, describing Meridian's own posture. Show the before and the after.
questionsV2.recallLine: An examiner asks how the acquirer satisfied itself about the acquired bank. Which pair evidences it?

optionsShort.B: Purchase agreement and its security clauses
optionsShort.C: Ridgeline's 2021 test and a remediation plan
optionsShort.D: Meridian's own record and unified policy

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: What shows that Meridian secured contractual protection in the transaction?

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: What did Ridgeline itself do about assurance before it was acquired?

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: What demonstrates that the combined entity now operates under one governance regime?

sources: NIST SP 800-161 Rev 1 (upd 1) | Section 3.1 C-SCRM in Acquisition
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SR-6 Supplier Assessments and Reviews
No NIST source defines due care / due diligence; recorded as a legal-liability concept

questionsV2.question: Two standards specify different minimum password lengths and both cite the same policy. Which action BEST resolves the conflict at its source?

options.A: Assign one owner to approve every standard, and reissue the two under that authority.
options.B: Adopt the stricter of the two lengths and update the weaker standard to match it.
options.C: Move the requirement into the policy so that the board's approval settles it.
options.D: Publish a guideline recommending the stricter length until the standards are rewritten.

questionsV2.explanation: Two standards contradict each other because two people were allowed to issue standards, and no choice between the two numbers changes that. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 makes the point structurally: every control family opens with a Policy and Procedures control, AC-1, AT-1, AU-1 and so on through SR-1, each requiring a documented policy, dissemination to defined roles, a designated official to manage its development and review, and review and update on a defined frequency and after defined events. NIST CSF 2.0 states the same in GV.PO-01 and GV.PO-02. Note that the policy, standard, procedure and guideline hierarchy itself, and the mandatory versus discretionary distinction, is CISSP-canon rather than NIST text. B is symptom not cause, resolving this contradiction and leaving the process that made it. C is wrong scope, pushing a parameter into a document meant to outlive parameters. D is the right control for a different problem, because a guideline is discretionary and cannot settle a mandatory requirement. Fix the authority, not the number.
questionsV2.recallLine: Two standards contradict each other on a parameter. What resolves the conflict at its source?

optionsShort.C: Move the number into the policy

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: What should the reissued standard say once a single owner has been appointed?

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: What belongs in a policy rather than in a standard beneath it?

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Which instrument is right for advice that teams may reasonably decline to follow?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | the '-1' Policy and Procedures control in every family (AC-1 through SR-1)
NIST CSF 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29) | GV.PO-01, GV.PO-02
NIST SP 800-18 Rev 1 | Section 3, plan development and structure

questionsV2.question: A director asks why the security plan classifies controls one way and the risk report another. Which explanation is MOST accurate?

options.A: The plan uses the catalogue's families because they are mandatory; the report's categories are optional.
options.B: The two are the same taxonomy under different names, so either may be used interchangeably.
options.C: The plan groups controls by family, while the report groups them by the function they serve.
options.D: The report's categories replaced the families when the bank adopted the newer framework.

questionsV2.explanation: These are two axes over the same controls, not two competing lists, and a director who understands that stops asking which one is right. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Chapter 2 organizes controls into twenty families and characterizes each by implementation responsibility, organization or system, and by whether it is a base control or an enhancement. It never classifies a control as preventive, detective or corrective. That functional taxonomy, together with deterrent, directive and compensating, is CISSP-canon and appears in no NIST publication. The one near-member is the compensating control, which lives in NIST SP 800-53B Chapter 2 as tailoring guidance rather than as a class of control. A is symptom not cause, asserting a status difference where both are descriptions of the same set. B is wrong scope, collapsing two organizing axes into one. D is wrong phase, implying a supersession that never happened. Know which axis a question is asking about.
questionsV2.recallLine: Why does one document group controls by family and another by preventive or detective function?

optionsShort.C: One groups by family, one by function

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Which control set is a US federal system actually obliged to implement?

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: When can two classification schemes be treated as interchangeable for reporting?

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: What did change between Revision 4 and Revision 5 of the control catalogue?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | Chapter 2, control structure, families and implementation responsibility
NIST SP 800-53B | Chapter 2, compensating controls in tailoring guidance
The preventive/detective/corrective taxonomy has no NIST source and is attributed to CISSP-canon material

questionsV2.question: Three hundred staff are changing roles as two branch regions merge. Which control MOST directly addresses the risk that creates?

options.A: Requiring every transferring employee to re-sign the acceptable use agreement.
options.B: Reviewing and revising each transferring employee's access to match the new role.
options.C: Disabling each transferring employee's account for the day the move takes effect.
options.D: Requiring managers to certify their team's access at the end of each quarter.

questionsV2.explanation: A transfer adds rights and almost never subtracts them, so 300 transfers produce 300 people holding two jobs' worth of access and one job's worth of need. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PS-5 Personnel Transfer is the control written for this: review and confirm the ongoing operational need for current logical and physical access authorizations when individuals are reassigned or transferred, initiate the resulting transfer or reassignment actions within a defined period, and modify access authorization as needed. PS-4 Personnel Termination handles the leavers and AC-2 Account Management the accounts themselves. A is the right control for a different problem, reaffirming the rules of behaviour while the entitlements ride along untouched. C is symptom not cause, an interruption rather than a revision, and the account comes back exactly as it was. D is detective when preventive is asked, finding accumulated access one quarter after it accumulated. Revise at the moment of the move.
questionsV2.recallLine: Three hundred staff change roles in a merger. Which control most directly addresses the risk?

optionsShort.B: Review and revise access to the new role
optionsShort.C: Disable the account for the move day

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: How does the bank refresh each employee's acknowledgement of the rules of behaviour?

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: How does the bank prevent access being used during an unsupervised handover window?

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: How does the bank catch entitlements that accumulated despite the transfer process?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PS-5 Personnel Transfer; PS-4 Personnel Termination; AC-2 Account Management

questionsV2.question: The awareness programme still teaches a threat catalogue written before the bank used any cloud service. Which change BEST fixes the underlying problem?

options.A: Add a cloud module to this year's curriculum and reissue the threat catalogue.
options.B: Replace the annual course with quarterly phishing simulations for all staff.
options.C: Have each business unit write the module that covers its own systems and threats.
options.D: Schedule a content review on a set cadence and after defined trigger events.

questionsV2.explanation: The content is stale because nothing in the programme has a date on which it expires, and adding one module leaves the same gap ready to reopen next year. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AT-2 Literacy Training and Awareness requires literacy training and awareness content to be updated on an organization-defined frequency and following organization-defined events, which is precisely the cadence-plus-trigger arrangement the option describes, and AT-3 Role-Based Training carries the same obligation for role-specific material. Note the Revision 5 title: AT-2 was called Security Awareness Training in Revision 4, so older material names it differently. NIST CSF 2.0 places the same idea under PR.AT. A is symptom not cause, patching this year's gap by the same means that produced it. B is the right control for a different problem, measuring susceptibility rather than refreshing content. C is not the decision-maker's, distributing authorship without establishing when anything gets reviewed. Give the content an expiry date.
questionsV2.recallLine: Awareness content predates the technology it should cover. What fixes the underlying problem?

optionsShort.A: Add a cloud module this year
optionsShort.C: Each unit writes its own module
optionsShort.D: Review on a cadence and on triggers

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: What should this year's curriculum include once a review cadence exists?

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: How does the bank measure whether awareness training is changing behaviour?

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: How can role-specific content stay accurate for systems the central team does not run?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AT-2 Literacy Training and Awareness (renamed from Rev 4 Security Awareness Training); AT-3 Role-Based Training
NIST CSF 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29) | PR.AT Awareness and Training

questionsV2.question: Meridian's wire-transfer system records the name of the officer who approved each payment. During a control walkthrough the auditor discovers that an administrator can edit those records afterwards, and that nothing in the system marks a record as having been changed. Which security objective does the gap MOST directly undermine?

options.A: Confidentiality, because the record can be read by staff who did not approve it.
options.B: Integrity, because the record can be altered and the alteration cannot be shown.
options.C: Availability, because the record cannot be relied on when the examiner needs it.
options.D: Authenticity, because the record no longer proves who was at the console.

questionsV2.explanation: The loss the stem describes is silent modification, and modification is integrity in either framing a candidate might be carrying. This is a place where the two framings differ and the difference is worth knowing. FIPS 199, Section 3, quoting 44 U.S.C. 3542, defines exactly three security objectives, and its integrity definition reads as guarding against improper information modification or destruction, and includes ensuring information non-repudiation and authenticity. The five pillars that add authenticity and non-repudiation as peers of confidentiality, integrity and availability are ISC2's framing, not FIPS 199's, so never cite FIPS 199 as the source of a five-pillar claim. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 supplies the control-level split where it is needed: SI-7 for information integrity, AU-9 Protection of Audit Information, and AU-10 Non-repudiation. A is wrong scope, describing reading where the stem describes editing. C is symptom not cause, naming the examiner's difficulty rather than the mechanism. D is the right control for a different problem, and under FIPS 199 it is inside integrity anyway. Read the loss, then name the objective.
questionsV2.recallLine: An approval record can be silently edited by an administrator. Which objective is undermined?

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Which objective is lost when payment approvals can be read by staff with no business need?

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Which objective is lost when the record cannot be produced at all during an examination?

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Which objective is at stake when an attacker signs a message as somebody else?

sources: FIPS 199 | Section 3, Security Objectives (three objectives; integrity includes non-repudiation and authenticity)
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SI-7 Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity; AU-9 Protection of Audit Information; AU-10 Non-repudiation

questionsV2.question: A Meridian customer disputes a $180,000 transfer, saying she never authorized it. The bank's records show a successful sign-in from a machine she has used before, and an approval recorded at 11:04. The dispute is heading for court, and Meridian is redesigning the approval step so a future dispute can be settled. Which control contributes MOST directly to that goal?

options.A: Recording the session with full packet capture retained for one year.
options.B: Requiring a one-time code sent to the customer's registered phone.
options.C: Restricting large transfers to sessions from previously seen devices.
options.D: Signing the instruction with a private key that the customer alone holds.

questionsV2.explanation: Non-repudiation needs evidence that only one party could have produced, and that rules out anything the bank could have produced too. A signature made with a key the customer alone holds leaves Meridian outside the set of possible authors, which is what makes the evidence survive a dispute. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-10 Non-repudiation is the control: protect against an individual falsely denying having performed an action, and provide the means to determine whether the individual took it. SC-23 Session Authenticity covers the related but distinct property of the session itself. FIPS 199 folds non-repudiation and authenticity into its integrity objective, so AU-10 and SC-23 are where the two are addressed separately. A is wrong scope, capturing what crossed the wire rather than who originated it. B is the right control for a different problem, since a code Meridian generated and Meridian verified is evidence Meridian could have manufactured. C is symptom not cause, lowering the chance of an unfamiliar actor without producing evidence. Ask who else could have made this.
questionsV2.recallLine: Which control best keeps a customer from credibly denying that they authorized a transfer?

optionsShort.A: Full packet capture kept a year
optionsShort.B: One-time code to the registered phone
optionsShort.D: Sign with a key only the customer holds

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: How does the bank reconstruct exactly what was transmitted during a disputed session?

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: How does the bank raise confidence that the person signing in is the account holder?

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: How does the bank reduce the chance of a transfer being made from an unfamiliar machine?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AU-10 Non-repudiation; SC-23 Session Authenticity
FIPS 199 | Section 3 (non-repudiation and authenticity sit inside the integrity objective)

questionsV2.question: Meridian's fraud team wants to embed a vendor's scoring library in an internal tool that will run inside the bank and never be distributed to customers. The library's licence requires derivative works to be published under the same terms, and the team has already written three weeks of code against it. Which action should the CISO require BEFORE the build proceeds?

options.A: A legal review of whether the tool becomes a derivative work under that licence.
options.B: A software composition scan listing every third-party component the tool will include.
options.C: A vendor attestation that the library contains no known security vulnerabilities.
options.D: An entry in the software inventory recording the library and its licence terms.

questionsV2.explanation: The question the licence raises is whether shipping this tool obliges Meridian to publish its own fraud-scoring logic, and that is a legal determination about a specific set of facts, not a security judgement. Getting it wrong is expensive in a way that a vulnerability is not. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CM-10 Software Usage Restrictions is the control that requires software and associated documentation to be used in accordance with contract agreements and copyright law, and that licence quantities be tracked and controlled. Be honest about the limits of that citation: copyright, patent, trademark and trade-secret law are the governing sources for intellectual property generally, none of them is a NIST publication, and CM-10 covers only the software-licence compliance sliver. B is correct but not first, an inventory of components that does not answer the question the licence poses. C is the right control for a different problem, a vulnerability question wearing licence clothing. D is wrong phase, recording a decision that has not been made. Ask a lawyer a legal question.
questionsV2.recallLine: A library's licence requires derivative works to be published. What should be required before building?

B.label: correct but not first
B.wouldAnswer: How does the team discover which third-party components and licences it has taken on?

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: What assurance is wanted about the security of a third-party component being adopted?

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: What record should exist once the library has been approved for use?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-10 Software Usage Restrictions
Intellectual property statute is the governing source and is not a NIST publication; CM-10 covers only software-licence compliance

questionsV2.question: Meridian is opening a development office abroad and plans to give its engineers there access to the source of its hardware security module integration, which implements the bank's key wrapping. The office opens in nine weeks, the engineers are already hired, and the programme manager has asked the CISO to confirm that nothing stops the repository being opened to them. Which requirement should be checked FIRST?

options.A: That the source is stored in a repository located outside the European Union.
options.B: That the engineers sign confidentiality agreements enforceable in the destination country.
options.C: That the encryption technology is authorized for export to that destination.
options.D: That the bank's data classification policy permits source code to leave the country.

questionsV2.explanation: Cryptographic software and the technology behind it are export-controlled goods, and a regulation is not something an internal policy or a contract can satisfy. The Export Administration Regulations, 15 CFR Parts 730 to 774, control the export of encryption software and technology through the Commerce Control List, principally Category 5 Part 2, Information Security; defence articles including some cryptographic and satellite technology sit instead under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations, 22 CFR Parts 120 to 130. One trap worth carrying into the exam: releasing controlled technology to a foreign person is treated as an export even when the release happens inside the United States, so hiring rather than offshoring does not avoid the question. Neither regulation is a NIST publication, and the specific answer depends on the Commerce Control List entry and any licence exception for the item, which has to be checked rather than assumed. A is wrong scope, a data-residency question. B is the right control for a different problem, since confidentiality is not authorization. D is not the decision-maker's, because internal classification cannot authorize what a regulation controls. Regulation outranks policy.
questionsV2.recallLine: Engineers abroad will get source implementing key wrapping. Which requirement is checked first?

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Where must personal data of EU residents be stored or transferred under Chapter V of the GDPR?

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: How does the bank protect trade secrets shared with staff in another jurisdiction?

D.label: not the decision-maker's
D.wouldAnswer: What internal rule governs which classification of material may be shared with an overseas office?

sources: Export Administration Regulations | 15 CFR Parts 730 to 774, Commerce Control List Category 5 Part 2 (Information Security)
ITAR | 22 CFR Parts 120 to 130, US Munitions List
Neither is a NIST publication; the standards map records this outline item as unmapped

questionsV2.question: Meridian suspects a branch manager of falsifying loan documents. Internal audit has pulled six files and the pattern is consistent, but the general counsel has not yet decided whether this ends in dismissal, in a civil claim to recover the losses, or in a referral to prosecutors. The security team has been asked to collect the manager's mailbox and workstation. Which approach to evidence is MOST appropriate now?

options.A: Handle it as an administrative matter and re-collect to a higher standard if it escalates.
options.B: Collect and document to the standard the strictest possible outcome would demand.
options.C: Refer it to law enforcement now so that the collection standard becomes theirs to set.
options.D: Collect what the disciplinary policy requires and no more until counsel advises.

questionsV2.explanation: Evidence cannot be re-collected to a higher standard later, because the thing that would have to be redone is the handling, and the handling has already happened. When the destination is unknown, the only safe assumption is the most demanding one. NIST SP 800-61 Rev 3, Section 2.3, makes this a preparation obligation: decide in advance what will be collected, by whom and to what standard, because those decisions cannot be made credibly after the fact. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-9 Protection of Audit Information, AU-11 Audit Record Retention and IR-4(12) Incident Handling | Malicious Code and Forensic Analysis are the supporting controls. Be aware of the sourcing limit: no held standard enumerates the administrative, criminal, civil and regulatory investigation types by their burdens of proof, which is a matter of legal procedure, and NIST SP 800-86 is the guide that covers forensic technique. A is wrong phase. C is not the decision-maker's, and it forecloses the administrative route. D is wrong scope, sizing collection to the least demanding outcome. Collect for the worst case you might end up in.
questionsV2.recallLine: The investigation may end in dismissal or prosecution. What standard should evidence be collected to?

optionsShort.C: Refer to police and let them set it
optionsShort.D: Only what the disciplinary policy needs

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: How should evidence be handled when the matter is definitively internal and will stay internal?

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: Who decides whether a suspected crime is reported to law enforcement, and when?

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: What is the minimum an employer must document to support a disciplinary decision?

sources: NIST SP 800-61 Rev 3 | Section 2.3 Incident Response Policies, Processes, and Procedures
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AU-9; AU-11 Audit Record Retention; IR-4(12) Malicious Code and Forensic Analysis
No held standard enumerates investigation types by burden of proof; SP 800-86 is the forensic-technique source

questionsV2.question: Meridian is filling three vacancies this month: a branch teller, a database administrator who will hold production access to the core banking platform, and a contract cleaner who will have unescorted after-hours access to the head office floors. HR has asked the CISO what background checking each of the three requires. Which approach to screening is MOST defensible?

options.A: Screen all three identically so the process cannot be challenged as inconsistent.
options.B: Screen the two employees to the bank's standard and exempt the contractor's employer.
options.C: Screen according to seniority, with the most senior of the three screened most thoroughly.
options.D: Assign each position a risk designation first, then screen against that designation.

questionsV2.explanation: Screening depth should follow what the position can reach, and that is a property of the job rather than of its title or its pay grade. The sequence is explicit in NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PS-2 Position Risk Designation: assign a risk designation to all organizational positions, establish screening criteria for individuals filling those positions, and review and update the designations on a defined frequency. PS-3 Personnel Screening then screens individuals prior to authorizing access and rescreens according to defined conditions, and PS-7 External Personnel Security extends the requirement to third-party personnel; note that PS-7 was titled Third-Party Personnel Security in Revision 4. A is wrong scope, one depth for a whole population regardless of reach. B is not the decision-maker's, delegating a decision to a supplier without setting the requirement, and the cleaner has the building at 3 a.m. C is symptom not cause, since seniority is a proxy for access and here it points away from the risk. Designate the position, then screen the person.
questionsV2.recallLine: Three roles with very different access are being hired. Which screening approach is most defensible?

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: What screening applies to a population of positions that genuinely share one risk designation?

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: How should a contractor's own screening obligations be established and evidenced?

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: When does seniority happen to be a reasonable proxy for the access a role carries?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PS-2 Position Risk Designation; PS-3 Personnel Screening
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PS-7 External Personnel Security (renamed from Rev 4 Third-Party Personnel Security)

questionsV2.question: Meridian's risk register lists phishing as a risk, scored with a likelihood of 4 and an impact of 5 by the operations manager who entered it. Preparing the quarterly report for the risk committee, an analyst argues that the entry cannot be assessed as written and should be sent back. What is the MOST accurate objection?

options.A: It names a threat without naming the vulnerability it would exploit or the asset harmed.
options.B: It names a control failure rather than a risk, so the entry belongs in the findings log.
options.C: It uses a qualitative likelihood where the register's own method requires a quantitative one.
options.D: It has no named owner, so nobody can be asked to reduce the likelihood it records.

questionsV2.explanation: Phishing is an event somebody might attempt, not a risk Meridian holds. A risk statement has to say what the attempt would exploit and what harm follows, because until it does, neither likelihood nor impact has anything to attach to and neither number is defensible. NIST SP 800-30 Rev 1, Chapter 3, models risk as a threat source initiating a threat event that exploits a vulnerability, producing an adverse impact, and its Appendix D and Appendix E supply the threat source and threat event taxonomies a register is populated from. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 RA-3 Risk Assessment is the control obligation behind it. B is wrong scope, recategorizing the entry rather than completing it. C is symptom not cause, a formatting objection that leaves an unassessable statement unassessable in a different notation. D is correct but not first, since ownership is genuinely required and does not make the entry assessable. Write the sentence with all its parts in it.
questionsV2.recallLine: A risk register entry reads only 'phishing' with a likelihood and impact. What is wrong with it?

optionsShort.B: It is a control failure, not a risk

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Where should an entry go that records a control that was found not to be operating?

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: What objection applies when a well-formed risk is scored in the wrong notation?

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: What is missing when a well-formed risk sits in the register with nobody accountable for it?

sources: NIST SP 800-30 Rev 1 | Chapter 3; Appendix D Threat Sources; Appendix E Threat Events
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | RA-3 Risk Assessment

questionsV2.question: Meridian's internal audit team has assessed the vendor access policy that was rewritten after the TechSafe breach, and its report says only that the policy is in place and has been distributed. The CISO returns the report, saying that is a statement about a document rather than an assessment result. What is MOST clearly missing?

options.A: The date the policy was approved and the official who approved it.
options.B: The number of vendors that the policy currently applies to.
options.C: Evidence that the policy operated as intended over the period examined.
options.D: A comparison of the policy against the equivalent control in the framework.

questionsV2.explanation: A control assessment answers three questions and existence is only the first of them. NIST SP 800-53A Rev 5 structures its assessment procedures around determining whether controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting the security and privacy requirements, and it applies the examine, interview and test methods to reach that determination. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CA-2 Control Assessments is the obligation to run them and to produce the assessment report. A policy that exists and is ignored fails the second and third questions, which is the situation Meridian was in with TechSafe's contract. A is wrong scope, provenance of the document rather than its operation. B is the right control for a different problem, the scope of applicability. D is wrong phase, a design comparison that precedes the question of whether the thing works. Existence is not effectiveness.
questionsV2.recallLine: An assessor reports that a policy is in place. What is missing from that as an assessment result?

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: What should the document register hold about each approved policy?

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: What does the CISO need to know to judge how much of the vendor estate a policy reaches?

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: What check confirms that the bank's policy set covers each control the framework requires?

sources: NIST SP 800-53A Rev 5 | assessment procedures and the examine, interview and test methods
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | CA-2 Control Assessments

questionsV2.question: Meridian assesses its controls once a year, in March, and the last assessment reported no significant findings. Since then the bank has migrated two applications to a cloud provider and has changed its vendor access model twice. At the December board meeting a director asks why an annual control assessment is not enough. Which answer BEST states the case for continuous monitoring?

options.A: It reduces the cost of assessment by spreading the same work across the year.
options.B: It keeps the authorization decision informed by the system's current state.
options.C: It satisfies the examiner's expectation of testing more often than annually.
options.D: It detects attacks sooner, because the monitoring is running all the time.

questionsV2.explanation: The point of monitoring controls continuously is that the decision to run the system rests on information that is still true. An annual assessment authorizes a system as it was in March and says nothing about the seven changes made since. NIST SP 800-137 defines information security continuous monitoring as maintaining ongoing awareness of information security, vulnerabilities and threats to support organizational risk management decisions, and NIST SP 800-37 Rev 2 makes the consequence explicit in its MONITOR step, where ongoing authorization replaces a point-in-time decision. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CA-7 Continuous Monitoring is the control. A is symptom not cause, a cost argument that would hold even if the information were worthless. C is not the decision-maker's, making the examiner the reason rather than the risk. D is the right control for a different problem, and it is the seductive answer: security control monitoring and intrusion detection are different activities, and SI-4 System Monitoring is where the second one lives. Monitor so the decision stays current.
questionsV2.recallLine: Why is an annual control assessment not sufficient? State the case for continuous monitoring.

optionsShort.A: Spreads assessment cost across the year

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: What is a secondary benefit of moving from one annual push to a steady assessment cadence?

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: What does the bank tell an examiner who asks how often controls are tested?

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: What does SI-4 System Monitoring provide that a control assessment does not?

sources: NIST SP 800-137 | information security continuous monitoring definition and process
NIST SP 800-37 Rev 2 | Chapter 3, MONITOR step and ongoing authorization
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | CA-7 Continuous Monitoring; SI-4 System Monitoring

questionsV2.question: An outside adviser reports Meridian at Tier 2 and recommends reaching Tier 4 within two years, at a cost the adviser has already estimated. The CISO has been asked to endorse the recommendation before it goes to the board in January, and nobody has yet written down what the bank needs. Which response BEST reflects how the framework is meant to be used?

options.A: Adopt Tier 4 as the target and budget the programme against the gap it implies.
options.B: Ask the consultant to reassess each business unit so the bank holds a Tier for each.
options.C: Benchmark the reported Tier against peer banks before accepting it as a target.
options.D: Set a target profile from the bank's own risk appetite, then read the Tier against it.

questionsV2.explanation: The framework's own improvement mechanism is the gap between a Current Profile and a Target Profile, and the Target Profile is derived from what the organization needs rather than from the top of a scale. NIST CSF 2.0, published as NIST CSWP 29, defines four Tiers, Partial, Risk Informed, Repeatable and Adaptive, describing the rigour of an organization's cybersecurity risk governance and risk management practices, and it is explicit that the Tiers are not maturity levels even though they are routinely used as if they were. A Tier read against a target the bank chose is diagnostic; a Tier treated as a score is a budget request. A is correct but not first, because a target is needed and taking the highest available as the target skips the step that decides what the bank requires. B is the right control for a different problem, resolution rather than direction. C is symptom not cause, since a peer's posture does not establish this bank's risk appetite. Decide what you need, then measure the distance.
questionsV2.recallLine: A consultant reports a Tier and recommends a higher one. How should the framework actually be used?

optionsShort.A: Adopt the top Tier as the target
optionsShort.D: Set a target profile, read the Tier against it

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: What does the programme do once a target has been chosen and the gap is understood?

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: How does a large organization get useful resolution when its units differ widely in practice?

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: How does a board judge whether its posture is unusual for an institution of its size?

sources: NIST CSF 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29) | the four Tiers and the Organizational Profile mechanism
NIST states the Tiers are not maturity levels; CMM and CMMI are not NIST publications

questionsV2.question: Meridian is examined against banking supervisory expectations, processes card data under the card brand rules, and reports to a European parent whose group audit committee asks for ISO alignment. The CISO has one control assessment team and a calendar that already carries three audits. Which approach to frameworks is MOST workable?

options.A: Pick one framework as the system of record and map the others onto it.
options.B: Run each framework separately so that every audience receives its own artefacts.
options.C: Adopt whichever framework has the most controls, so the others are covered by it.
options.D: Let each business unit choose the framework that its own regulator names.

questionsV2.explanation: Three audiences do not require three programmes; they require one set of controls and three views of it, because a control assessed once can be reported many times but a control assessed three ways is assessed badly three times. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-9 Risk Management Strategy requires a single organization-wide strategy, and NIST SP 800-37 Rev 2 Chapter 3 gives the RMF steps that a mapped control set resolves into, with NIST SP 800-53B supplying the baselines. NIST CSF 2.0's Organizational Profile is itself designed as the mapping surface. Two of the frameworks named here, ISO/IEC 27005 and COBIT, are paywalled, so a reader should expect to buy them rather than follow a link. B is the right control for a different problem, satisfying audiences at the cost of one coherent risk picture. C is symptom not cause, because control count is not coverage and each framework's set is selected against its own scope. D is wrong scope, fragmenting a strategy the organization is meant to hold once. One system of record, many reports.
questionsV2.recallLine: Three audiences demand three frameworks. What is the most workable way to organize the programme?

optionsShort.A: One system of record, map the rest
optionsShort.C: Adopt the one with most controls
optionsShort.D: Each unit picks its regulator's framework

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: How does the bank produce artefacts in the exact format each audience expects?

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: When is a larger control set genuinely the right starting point for a programme?

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: How should a unit with a unique regulatory obligation extend the common control set?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PM-9 Risk Management Strategy
NIST SP 800-37 Rev 2 | Chapter 3, the RMF steps; NIST SP 800-53B baselines
NIST CSF 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29) | Organizational Profile as a mapping mechanism
Neither ISO/IEC 27005 nor COBIT is held here; both are paywalled

questionsV2.question: Meridian's team is modelling threats to a new mobile deposit feature before any code is written. The session opens with each engineer listing attacks they have read about in the last year, and after forty minutes the list is long, nobody has opened the design, and the architect is losing patience. Which starting point would make the model MOST useful?

options.A: The vulnerabilities the last penetration test found in the existing mobile application.
options.B: The feature's data flows and the trust boundaries that each flow crosses.
options.C: The controls the bank already runs, so that gaps show up against them.
options.D: The threat intelligence feed's current list of campaigns against retail banks.

questionsV2.explanation: A threat model is a model of the system, and a list of remembered attacks is a model of the team. Starting from data flows and trust boundaries forces the exercise to enumerate the places where something crosses from one level of trust to another, which is where attacks land whether or not anyone has read about them. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SA-8 Security and Privacy Engineering Principles names threat modelling in its discussion as the means of identifying use cases, threat agents, attack vectors and patterns, and SA-11(2) Developer Testing and Evaluation | Threat Modeling and Vulnerability Analyses requires it at defined breadth and depth. NIST SP 800-218 PW.1.1 puts risk modelling at design time, before code exists, so the design itself can still change. Note that STRIDE, PASTA and DREAD are named throughout CISSP study material and appear in no NIST publication. A is wrong phase, starting from findings against a system that already exists. C is symptom not cause, modelling the defence rather than the thing defended. D is wrong scope, and a model built from current campaigns expires with them. Model the system, then populate it with threats.
questionsV2.recallLine: A team starts threat modelling from remembered attacks. What starting point makes the model useful?

optionsShort.A: Findings from the last penetration test

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: What should drive remediation planning for the mobile application already in production?

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: How does the bank establish which of its existing controls the new feature can inherit?

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: What keeps a completed threat model current as adversary behaviour changes?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SA-8 Security and Privacy Engineering Principles; SA-11(2) Threat Modeling and Vulnerability Analyses
NIST SP 800-218 | PW.1.1 risk modelling at design time
STRIDE, PASTA and DREAD appear in no NIST publication and are attributed to CISSP-canon material

questionsV2.question: The browser console hides the cash-limit field from any user whose role is not permitted to change it. Which finding about that console design is MOST serious?

options.A: Authorization is enforced in console code the user controls, not on the server.
options.B: The console is served over TLS 1.2 rather than TLS 1.3, which weakens the transport.
options.C: The console hides the field with client script instead of a server-rendered template.
options.D: The console does not write cash-limit changes to the bank's central audit repository.

questionsV2.explanation: Anything a browser enforces is advice. The user owns the machine, the script and the request, so a hidden field can be restored from a developer console or the request replayed with the field set, and Nexus has no server-side objection ready. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-3 Access Enforcement puts the obligation on the system to enforce approved authorizations, and OWASP Top 10:2025 lists enforcement that happens only on the client under A01 Broken Access Control. B is a real transport finding and the right control for a different problem: TLS protects the request from a third party on the wire and does nothing about the party sending it. C is symptom not cause, because a server-rendered page hides the field more tidily and the server still accepts whatever arrives. D is detective when preventive is asked; the log would name whoever raised a limit, after the cash left. Decide where enforcement runs before deciding how the interface looks.
questionsV2.recallLine: A browser console hides a privileged field by role. What is the most serious design finding?

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Which transport setting should be raised when the concern is a third party reading the session?

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: How should a field be hidden once the server already enforces the rule?

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: What is missing if the question is how the bank would later prove who changed a limit?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-3 Access Enforcement
OWASP Top 10:2025 | A01 Broken Access Control

questionsV2.question: The migration will lift the existing server image into the new environment unchanged, including services nobody has used in three years. Which action BEST reduces the attack surface it carries across?

options.A: Run an authenticated vulnerability scan against the image and remediate the findings it reports.
options.B: Place the server behind a firewall that inspects traffic to each of its listening ports.
options.C: Rebuild the image from a documented baseline limited to the services the platform needs.
options.D: Deploy host-based intrusion detection so an unused service raises an alert when it is touched.

questionsV2.explanation: A three-year-old service nobody uses is not a vulnerability to be patched, it is a capability that should not be there. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CM-7 Least Functionality requires the system to be configured to provide only mission-essential capabilities, with defined functions, ports, protocols and services prohibited or restricted, and CM-2 Baseline Configuration is where that configuration is recorded and held. A is correct but not first: a scan tells Nexus what is listening and removes none of it, and it will report on services that should have been deleted rather than fixed. B is the right control for a different problem, because boundary filtering governs who reaches a port, not whether the port should exist at all, and the shared cluster puts plenty of traffic inside the boundary. D is detective when preventive is asked and accepts the service as permanent. Remove capability first, then defend what is left.
questionsV2.recallLine: A legacy server image moves unchanged into a new environment. What best reduces the surface it carries?

optionsShort.A: Scan the image and remediate findings
optionsShort.B: Firewall in front of listening ports
optionsShort.C: Rebuild from a minimal documented baseline
optionsShort.D: Host intrusion detection on unused services

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: How would the team discover which unused services the image is actually running?

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: What protects a service that must keep running but should be reachable only from named networks?

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: What gives warning if a service that cannot be removed is used unexpectedly?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-7 Least Functionality
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-2 Baseline Configuration

questionsV2.question: The application tier will pull its base images from a public registry at build time. Which control MOST directly addresses the risk that introduces?

options.A: Network policy restricting which pods in the cluster may open connections to each other.
options.B: Verification of a digital signature on every image before the cluster is allowed to run it.
options.C: Scanning each built image for known-vulnerable packages before it is promoted to production.
options.D: A read-only root filesystem in each container so a compromised process cannot write to disk.

questionsV2.explanation: Pulling from a public registry means the cluster runs whatever answers to a name and a tag, and both are attacker-controllable in a way a version number is not. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CM-14 Signed Components requires the organization to prevent installation of defined components without verification that the component was signed with a certificate the organization recognizes and approves, and SR-4 Provenance and SR-11 Component Authenticity carry the supply-chain half of the same obligation. NIST's dedicated container publication is SP 800-190; the control obligation above stands on its own. A is the right control for a different problem, lateral movement once a pod is compromised. C is symptom not cause: it finds known-bad packages inside an image whose origin is still unverified, so a purpose-built malicious image with current packages passes. D is wrong phase, limiting what a running container can do after an unverified image has already been admitted. Decide what is allowed to run before deciding how it may behave.
questionsV2.recallLine: Base images come from a public registry at build time. Which control most directly addresses that risk?

optionsShort.C: Scan built images for known CVEs

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: What limits how far an attacker moves once one pod is compromised?

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: How does the team find images carrying package versions with published vulnerabilities?

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: What reduces the damage a compromised container process can do at runtime?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-14 Signed Components
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SR-4 Provenance; SR-11 Component Authenticity
NIST SP 800-190 (Application Container Security Guide), named as the dedicated source

questionsV2.question: The architects note that the provider patches the function runtime and isolates tenants. Given that division, which control should the bank's own review focus on MOST?

options.A: Hardening the guest operating system image the reconciliation functions run inside.
options.B: Agreeing an availability service level for the overnight reconciliation window.
options.C: Scheduling a quarterly vulnerability scan of the provider's platform endpoints.
options.D: Scoping each function's execution role to the permissions it actually needs.

questionsV2.explanation: When the provider owns the host, the runtime and the tenant boundary, what is left for Nexus to get wrong is the identity the function runs as and what that identity may reach. A function with a broad role is a standing credential that executes on a schedule with nobody watching. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6 Least Privilege requires access authorizations to be no more than necessary for assigned tasks, and SA-9 External System Services requires the organization to define and document the roles and responsibilities of external providers rather than assume them, which is what makes the division above a contractual fact instead of a hope. A is not the decision-maker's: there is no guest image here that Nexus owns. B is the right control for a different problem, an availability commitment rather than a security surface. C is wrong scope, testing someone else's platform where the bank has neither authorization nor residual risk. Ask what the provider has not taken away.
questionsV2.recallLine: A provider patches the runtime and isolates tenants. Where should the bank's own review concentrate?

A.label: not the decision-maker's
A.wouldAnswer: What would the bank harden if it had chosen to run these jobs on its own virtual machines?

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: What should the contract say if the concern is the reconciliation finishing before branches open?

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: What testing does the bank owe on the systems it operates and is authorized to test?

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-6 Least Privilege
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SA-9 External System Services

questionsV2.question: The dispenser-control service will run as a hypervisor guest and the team plans to keep a snapshot of every release. Which practice MOST reduces the risk that arrangement creates?

options.A: Encrypting the guest's virtual disk so its contents are unreadable if the file is copied.
options.B: Restricting access to the hypervisor management console to a named administrator group.
options.C: Enrolling every guest and retained snapshot in the same inventory and patching programme as physical hosts.
options.D: Taking a fresh snapshot before every change so the service can be rolled back quickly.

questionsV2.explanation: A guest is created by an API call and a snapshot by a menu item, so virtual estates grow faster than the processes that are supposed to govern them, and a snapshot is a complete machine holding whatever data it held on the day it was taken. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CM-8 System Component Inventory requires an inventory that accurately reflects the system and is updated as components are installed or removed, CM-2 Baseline Configuration governs what each of those components should look like, and SA-22 Unsupported System Components is what a forgotten legacy guest eventually becomes. Note that the catalogue contains no hypervisor-specific control; the obligation rides on the general ones. A is the right control for a different problem, protecting a disk file at rest. B is wrong scope, governing who administers the platform rather than the population of guests that accumulates on it. D is wrong phase and makes the problem larger, because it is a rollback measure that manufactures more of the artefacts the stem is worried about. Count the machines before hardening them.
questionsV2.recallLine: A legacy service runs as a hypervisor guest and every release is snapshotted. What most reduces the risk?

optionsShort.C: Inventory and patch guests and snapshots

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: What protects a virtual disk copied off the datastore by someone with storage access?

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: What limits who can create, clone or destroy guests on the platform?

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: What lets the team undo a bad change to the dispenser-control service quickly?

questionsV2.question: The programme board asks how the SlimLine II's control set should be arrived at. Which sequence BEST describes a defensible selection?

options.A: Adopt the control set the previous SlimLine programme used, then add controls for the new interface.
options.B: Categorize the system by impact, take the matching baseline, then tailor it with documented justification.
options.C: Take the highest baseline available and remove the controls the examiner agrees are not applicable.
options.D: Ask the examiner which controls it expects to see and build the set from that answer.

questionsV2.explanation: Selection is a chain, and each link supplies the reason for the next. FIPS 199 Section 3 categorizes the system by the impact a loss of confidentiality, integrity or availability would have. FIPS 200 Section 3 turns that category into an obligation to apply the corresponding minimum controls. NIST SP 800-53B Chapters 2 and 3 supply the Low, Moderate and High baselines and the tailoring guidance, and SP 800-53 Rev 5 made both steps auditable in their own right with PL-10 Baseline Selection and PL-11 Baseline Tailoring. SP 800-37 Rev 2 Section 3.3 walks the same ground as RMF tasks S-1 through S-6. A is wrong scope: the old set was selected against the old terminal's categorization, and the new one has a different interface and a different impact. C is wrong phase, using tailoring in place of selection so that nothing states what the system needs. D is not the decision-maker's; the system owner categorizes and selects, and the examiner assesses what was done. Categorize first, and the argument writes itself.
questionsV2.recallLine: How should a new terminal's control set be arrived at so the choice can be defended?

optionsShort.A: Reuse the previous programme's control set
optionsShort.B: Categorize, take baseline, tailor with justification
optionsShort.C: Start highest and subtract by agreement
optionsShort.D: Build from what the examiner names

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: What is a reasonable starting draft when two systems share a categorization and an environment?

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: What does an organization do after a baseline has been selected and some controls do not fit?

D.label: not the decision-maker's
D.wouldAnswer: Who determines whether the selected controls were implemented and are working?

FIPS 200 | Section 3, Minimum Security Requirements
NIST SP 800-53B | Chapters 2 and 3, baselines and tailoring
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PL-10 Baseline Selection; PL-11 Baseline Tailoring
NIST SP 800-37 Rev 2 | Section 3.3 SELECT, tasks S-1 to S-6

questionsV2.question: The new dispenser interface and the existing transaction switch were built by different teams against the same written specification. Which activity is MOST likely to expose a defect neither team's own testing found?

options.A: A static analysis run over each team's source code against the bank's coding standard.
options.B: A penetration test of the assembled terminal conducted after it has entered production.
options.C: A design review comparing each team's architecture document with the approved specification.
options.D: Integration testing of the assembled interfaces against cases where the two readings disagree.

questionsV2.explanation: Two teams reading one specification produce two specifications, and the gap between them is invisible to any test that examines one side alone. NIST SP 800-160 Vol 1 Rev 1 Appendix H.8 Integration is the lifecycle process that synthesizes system elements into a realized system, and it is precisely where interface and composition weaknesses surface, because it is the first activity that exercises the seam rather than the parts. SP 800-53 Rev 5 CA-3 Information Exchange governs the resulting connection; note that Rev 5 renamed it from the Rev 4 title System Interconnections, so material still using the older name is dated. A is wrong scope, testing each element on the terms each team already passed. B is wrong phase, arriving after the terminal is live and after the cheapest moment to fix a seam has gone. C is the right control for a different problem, comparing documents with a document while the defect lives in behaviour. Test the joint, not the pieces.
questionsV2.recallLine: Two teams built either side of one interface from one specification. What best exposes a seam defect?

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: What finds coding-standard violations and common weaknesses inside one team's own source?

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: What validates the assembled terminal against an adversary once it is fielded?

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: What confirms that each team's intended architecture matches what was approved?

sources: NIST SP 800-160 Vol 1 Rev 1 | Appendix H.8 Integration
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | CA-3 Information Exchange (renamed from Rev 4 System Interconnections)

questionsV2.question: Fifty SlimLine II units are ready and the board wants them in service this quarter. Which condition should the security lead insist on BEFORE the first unit is cut over?

options.A: A documented back-out procedure and the retained configuration the units would be restored to.
options.B: A signed statement from the vendor that the units meet the approved specification.
options.C: A penetration test report covering the units in their final production configuration.
options.D: An updated asset inventory listing each unit's serial number and installation site.

questionsV2.explanation: Cutover is the moment a design becomes an operating system, and the only property that makes it survivable is reversibility. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CM-2(3) Baseline Configuration | Retention of Previous Configurations exists for exactly this, requiring a defined number of previous baseline versions to be retained to support rollback, and its discussion counts hardware, software, firmware, configuration files and records among them. NIST SP 800-160 Vol 1 Rev 1 Appendix H.10 Transition frames the wider obligation: preserve the system's verified security characteristics through an orderly, planned move into the operational environment. B is not the decision-maker's; a vendor statement is evidence the bank weighs, not the bank's own gate. C is wrong phase, because verification belongs earlier in the lifecycle and a report is not a way back. D is the right control for a different problem, since an inventory is needed to operate the fleet and does nothing to make the first fifty reversible. Never move something you cannot move back.
questionsV2.recallLine: Fifty new terminals are ready to cut over. What condition should the security lead insist on first?

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: What does the bank ask a supplier to provide as evidence in the acceptance pack?

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: What belongs at the verification gate, before units are declared ready?

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: What does operations need in order to maintain and account for the fielded fleet?
